name: go-imap-f68ef419-blind30-ots
instr:
# go-imap: a client and server giving wrong answers all over the protocol, without a test suite

Driving the sample mail service that ships here from the calling library in the same checkout, nearly every command path now answers wrongly in some way. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the callers changed; the same exchanges that used to be served correctly are now served wrongly, and in several places a command that used to succeed is refused outright. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Getting a session going. Signing in with a PLAIN credential exchange no longer works at all: the call reports a failure and the link never reaches the signed-in state. The bytes put on the wire during that exchange are inverted too — an empty step goes out as payload data and a data step as the empty placeholder. The answering side mishandles the same exchange from the other direction: a peer that supplies its own mechanism handling is pushed down the built-in PLAIN path instead, while a peer without that support is asked to do the handling it cannot do, and the exchange collapses. Upgrading a freshly opened plaintext link to an encrypted one before signing in fails as well: asking for the upgrade comes back as an error, so a plain no-op issued afterwards never gets the chance to run.

Opening a mailbox and asking what is in it. Opening the inbox reports that it holds nothing, although one item is present, and adding a new item to a mailbox fails out
